# Round 8 implementation — engine replacement: tokenization delegated to bash itself

**Commit:** `288017f6d7fc06637c0af182924d9ee97b787c1f` (branch `issue-2387`, pushed; parent `a7ba37166f3c0b02d7582f140ccc3dac2148b826`)

**Status:** SUCCESS — both r7 BLOCKERs closed, NIT closed; all three concerns marked addressed at round 8.

## Design decision: Option B

Tokenization is delegated to the installed bash via `bash --pretty-print` — a parse-only mode that builds the real parse tree and prints the program bash would execute, with comments discarded by the parser itself. `scan_execution_sites` runs the UNCHANGED site regex (`_EXEC_SITE`) and exact-prefix regex (`_BOUND_PREFIX_RE`) over that rendering; the file keeps only the bounded-push assertion it owns (exact prefix, every match, exact per-wrapper counts, shell-valid whitespace — all five axes preserved verbatim).

Why B over A and C:

- **Against C (line-scoped + two more members):** rounds 4–7 each closed an enumerated member set and were falsified by the next round's measured member (substitution `)` → case-pattern `)` / escapes / regex groups → backticks / nested defaults / ANSI-C → arrays / extglob / multi-line state). Five consecutive rounds is the finding: the class is bash's grammar itself, and any hand enumeration re-opens on the next unenumerated paren context or line-boundary rule. I cannot defend "closed this time" on the same argument shape four prior rounds shipped.
- **Against A (hand lexer, whole-document):** persistent state + continuation joining + heredoc-operator tracking + array/extglob modeling is a substantial re-derivation of bash's tokenizer — exactly the enumeration approach with a larger enumeration. The round-9 member (coproc, `for ((;;))`, `$[...]`, `[[ ( ) ]]` grouping, …) is predictable in kind if not in name.
- **For B:** the only tokenizer guaranteed to agree with bash is bash. `--pretty-print` uses the SAME grammar and binary that executes the wrappers (5.1.16 on this VM). Zero new dependencies — no uv.lock/pyproject change (the alternatives, `bashlex` (unmaintained, no `[[ ]]`/array support) and tree-sitter-bash (two new deps, error-tolerant parses), were both considered and rejected). Fail-loud is structural: anything bash cannot parse exits non-zero → ValueError carrying origin + bash's own source-line diagnosis. Non-execution is verified (canary probe) and PINNED by `test_rendering_never_executes` — load-bearing because the two watch scripts' terminal arms rewrite the real crontab.

## What each finding turned into

1. **`unmodeled-paren-context-fail-open` (BLOCKER) → CLOSED.** Array assignments and conditional extglob parse under bash's grammar (bash enables extended patterns while parsing `[[ ]]`), so their pushes appear in the rendering and are counted; extglob assignment OUTSIDE `[[ ]]` needs a runtime `shopt` a parse-only rendering never executes, so it refuses loudly (disclosed false-refusal cost, taken deliberately). There is no paren-context enumeration left to be incomplete.
2. **`multiline-shell-state-fail-open` (BLOCKER) → CLOSED** (modeled, not refused — with the EOF residue refused). Whole-document parse: `\` continuations are joined before tokenizing; a multi-line `$(...)`'s closing-line push is counted; UNCLOSED quote/substitution/heredoc at EOF is a bash parse error → loud refusal. r7's "refusing at EOL would false-refuse the wrappers' own multi-line substitutions" objection dissolves: whole-document parsing refuses only genuinely unclosed state, and all six wrappers render with zero refusals. **Commit:** `89d4a691915ab26311c1842299fda7c9c5150fda` (branch `issue-2387`, on r9 tip `ffed40e240c9e0aec03ab7d26096decf8e1638dd`; pushed)

### Design chosen and why

The single rule both reviewers' blockers reduce to, per the round-10 brief (Claude's proposed shape, preferred there): **a confirmed skip region may contain NEITHER a push reference NOR any `<<` text — either finding refuses loudly at region establishment.** Implemented as `_PUSH_REF` (matches `$PUSH`/`${PUSH}`/`$TELEGRAM_PUSH`/`${TELEGRAM_PUSH}`, escaped `\$PUSH` included at its `$`; word-bounded so `$PUSH_TIMEOUT`/`${PUSH_TIMEOUT}` do NOT match — measured, fixture N5 below) plus a raw `"<<" in line` check over `lines[idx+1 .. terminator]`, after the terminator is located, before any skip.
